newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian share volumes dry up, movement seen small.
newsitem.headline: Russian share volumes dry up, movement seen small.

text.p: Russian shares pulled back from a morning slide but ended down on a low $8 million volume as Western orders dried up and market initiative switched to local brokers, traders said on Wednesday.

The Russian Trading System index closed down one percent at 163.90. Mosenergo and UES were the only shares to trade more than $1 million. Mosenergo closed at $0.866 after $0.878 at Tuesday's close. UES closed at $0.0721 after $0.0726.

"If there is any movement it is going to be between bid and offer," said one Western analyst, who, like many, said the market was slowing down during the wait before President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery, expected in a few weeks.
"The market is not being driven by Western orders but by the speculative inclinations of local operators," said UCB's Dmitry Yevenko, who expected Mosenergo and LUKoil to gain on Thursday.
Alfa Capital's Kristen Burton Steiner predicted St. Petersburg Telephone, which split 30-for-1 on Wednesday, would go up in the near term.
A local offering of new stock was cancelled on Wednesday in order to make the offering on a national basis, a good sign for investors' interests, she said.

The government has frozen some of Gazprom's assets due to non-payment of taxes but shares of the monopoly, which is expected to announce conditions of an internation share placement in a few days, rose sharply to $0.355 after $0.321.
